course.title: Stars, Galaxies, and the Universe
course.description: Introduces stellar properties, stellar evolution, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way, galaxy classification, galaxy evolution, large-scale structure, dark matter, dark energy, and the observational foundations of modern cosmology.

status.reviewStatus: Approved for review release; not yet approved for instructional use

cadence.rationale: Matched 1:1 biweekly cadence: each lab and its paired problem set both follow the same two-lecture unit (see syllabus.html Lab and Problem-Set Cadence).

dataProvenance.src: materials/ASTR230/src/generate_astr230_content.py and generate_astr230_labs_psets.py generate all worked examples, lecture slides/notes, labs, and problem sets programmatically from shared constants.
realData: Sirius B mass/radius/luminosity/temperature (Bond et al. 2017 ApJ 840, 70; Hipparcos parallax) - verified via live web fetch this session.

Nearby/bright star catalog values (Sirius A, Vega, Rigel, Betelgeuse, Proxima Centauri, Alpha Centauri A, Barnard's Star, the Sun, and others) used for the Lab 01/02 HR-diagram and distance-modulus sample - standard Hipparcos-era literature values, not independently re-verified via live fetch this session; flagged for human spot-check in reference-log.md.
Milky Way rotation curve values (Lab 05) - representative of published flat rotation curve (~220-235 km/s, R = 5-25 kpc; e.g. Eilers et al. 2019, Sofue 2020) - flagged for spot-check.
Galaxy morphological classifications (Lab 06: M31, M87, M101, M104, M82, NGC 1300) - well-documented public astronomical facts - flagged for spot-check.

Five-cluster Hubble diagram data (Lab 07: Virgo, Ursa Major, Corona Borealis, Bootes, Hydra) - classic pedagogical redshift-distance data set reproduced in many introductory textbooks - flagged for spot-check against the adopted edition or NED.
